title: Chinese Dumplings Began as Medicine, Not Food | China Travel Expert
description:
By legend, China's dumplings weren't invented as food at all — they started as medicine, about 1,800 years ago.

The story goes that the Eastern Han physician Zhang Zhongjing wrapped lamb and warming herbs in dough, shaped like little ears — "jiao'er," tender ears — and gave them to villagers to cure frostbitten ears in winter. Over centuries they became jiaozi. The name echoes "jiaozi" (交子), the turning point between the old year and the new, which is why families fold and eat them at New Year's Eve midnight — and their shape mimics old silver ingots, a small wish for wealth in the year ahead. (The Zhang Zhongjing origin is a beloved legend, not documented history.)

🧭 Expert Tip: Pleat the edge of each wrapper instead of just pressing it flat — a sealed pleat is what keeps the dumpling from bursting in the boil.

饺子本是御寒的“娇耳”——医食同源，团圆一口。
